A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching methods, experiments, and appendices A–G. Text, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison. v2 adds Appendix H.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-identification experiments, parameter-recovery results, measured small-dimension fitting times, and validation and smoothing analyses in Appendices F–G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Figures 3–6 and 11 and the synthetic parameter-recovery check in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The verification procedure, ellipse extraction, and layer-normalization adaptation in Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. Appendix H discusses transformations without introducing a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the Pile-based recovery experiment, model-attribution task, synthetic validation, and smoothing scenarios. Appendix H does not report evaluations on truncated, temperature-scaled, or quantized outputs.

E2.justification: The comparisons involving linear signatures and SVD-based versus ellipse-specific fitting are retained. New Table 2 classifies attribution methods conceptually; it does not add evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Shared-token projection, the 1-million-parameter model with hidden size 64 and epsilon 0.00001, recovery metrics, and timing measurements over dimensions 8–256 remain unchanged. No experimental protocol is revised.

E4.justification: The sample-count analysis in Figure 5, synthetic check in Appendix F, and smoothing analysis in Appendix G/Figure 11 are retained. Appendix H adds explanatory discussion, without new robustness tests or analytical results supported by experiments.

E5.justification: Figure 3 continues to report mean distances with shaded standard errors. No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures are added or changed.

E6.justification: The empirical plots, numerical findings, and Table 1 estimates are unchanged. For example, Figure 5 retains terminal stretch MSE 0.0157, bias MSE 0.146, and rotation distance 0.312. Table 2 is a conceptual comparison rather than new empirical results.

T1.justification: Section 3 adds an explicit formal forgery definition using observed outputs and a black-box verifier f, requiring a new output that satisfies f(x)=1. The ellipse derivations, complexity arguments, and Appendix D proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract now limits practical infeasibility to currently known methods. The introduction explicitly distinguishes forgery resistance from unforgeability and acknowledges that attacks avoiding ellipse fitting cannot be ruled out. The four signature properties and main contributions are retained.

C2.justification: New Appendix H discusses the loss of the surface constraint under top-k truncation, claimed detectability under constant temperature, and expected preservation when the model head is not quantized. These extend applicability qualifications without empirical validation. The security discussion also makes the unknown-attack limitation more explicit.

D1.justification: CVXPY/MOSEK implementation details, CPU hardware, experimental parameters, and access assumptions are retained. The new footnote explaining that one generation step includes the full next-token distribution clarifies an input already specified mathematically.

R1.justification: Table 2 extends the explicit property comparison, including assigning forgery resistance to text watermarks and compactness to cryptographic methods. The cited works and overall research positioning are retained; bibliography changes otherwise update publication metadata.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose edits, replaces many uses of ellipsoid with ellipse, adds clarifying footnotes, acknowledgements, and Appendix H, and updates the publication header. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 and relocates several figures and Algorithm 1. Figure 2 loses its small geometric sketches, and Figure 4 moves its zoomed inset. Figures 2 and 4 also acquire stray gray number labels. Existing result displays otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 better aligns its headline security claim with caveats already present in v1 by restricting infeasibility to currently known methods. The formal forgery definition, comparison table, and applicability discussion modestly improve clarity. The new transformation claims remain untested, and small figure artifacts reduce presentation quality, limiting the overall gain.
